name: Automated Tender Notice
vera_note: A procurement system, still sending offers. To no addresses that exist anymore. The syntax is perfect.

glean.confident_output: Government procurement record. Request for tender, infrastructure maintenance contract.
glean.actual_output: Automated procurement system. Request for tender issued at 14:02:07. Recipient list: [217 addresses]. Delivery status: BOUNCED x217. System continued issuing at 24-hour intervals. Last issue: [DATE_CORRUPTED]. Total cycles: [CORRUPTED]. The recipient addresses ceased to exist before the first cycle completed.

lattice.interpretation: This system was set to run indefinitely pending contract award confirmation. Without a confirmation or cancellation signal, the standard loop continued. The loop was not a malfunction — it was doing exactly what it was told. The question is whether anyone told it to stop.

verification_result: Both tools correct. The procurement system ran unattended for an estimated 47 years before a power failure ended the cycle. No award was ever issued. No cancellation was ever received. It was still waiting.
